body.target_estimand: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})\}\), with numerical duplicates removed; this is the full-view coefficient equivalence class over component-aligned Gaussian completions of the arbitrary observed view graph.

sampling_model.design: At population level, the observed view graph records every view marginal and exactly the paired cross-covariance blocks on its edges. At sample level, each observed edge has a sourcewise-iid paired sample from that target pair marginal, and every view has a sourcewise-iid marginal sample; all sources refer to the same target law.
sampling_model.units: Observations are independent and identically distributed within each edge or marginal source. No independence between sources is required: cohorts may overlap, and an edge observation may also contribute to one or both marginal estimators. Signal-dependent enrollment, selection, and transport from source-specific populations are excluded.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable; the causal target is the graph-compatible full-view structural coefficient set and the ancestry common to every compatible completion.
sampling_model.overlap: Alignment is required only within each observed edge source. Every edge-joint covariance and every marginal covariance must be positive definite for Gaussian whitening. No nonedge cross-view block is observed or used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each edge-joint and marginal covariance receives a simultaneous empirical operator-norm region with multiplicity \(|E_{\mathrm{obs}}|+m\). Modified-Cholesky coefficients, residual blocks, completion values, and compatible sets are recomputed throughout the graph-moment region.

The multi-domain linear-SEM procedure exploits shared causal structure and domain-wise heterogeneity to recover a common graph from separate domain datasets.
Its pair condition is sufficient for full linear-model identification and worst-case necessary when intervention experiments observe overlapping variable sets.

body.tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, a candidate common order is compatible with an arbitrary observed view graph exactly when every observed-edge residual cross-block is diagonal and every coordinatewise partial disturbance covariance admits a positive-definite completion. The signed completion value \(\chi_G\) makes this second condition computable and stable. A new arbitrary-graph covariance-region inversion combines one sourcewise-iid paired sample per observed edge with every view marginal, without requiring cross-source independence; away from explicit feasibility and path-product margins it gives confidence-set coverage, Hausdorff coefficient-set consistency, and exact graph-essential-poset recovery. The generic elbow still shows that one preassigned view pair generically identifies the full coefficient tuple, and the memoized removed-set recursion retains its \(2^p\)-state compatibility guarantee. Duplicate-free numerical tuple enumeration beyond compatible-order enumeration is not claimed.

project_justification.gap: Existing multi-view LiMVAM identification results concern fully paired views under disturbance-diversity conditions, while general set-inference and Gaussian-DAG results do not handle a graph of paired covariance sources whose residual restrictions must also admit global positive-definite disturbance completion. In particular, edgewise residual diagonality and local edge positivity do not control nonchordal completion boundaries or provide finite-sample coefficient-set and common-ancestry guarantees.
project_justification.niche: For the component-aligned Gaussian subclass, each candidate order determines every view-specific coefficient matrix from that view's marginal covariance. Observed edges then determine partial coordinatewise disturbance covariances. The extraction map \(A_G\), its zero-fill right inverse \(E_G\), and the signed value \(\chi_G\) separate observable residual diagonality, global noise feasibility, and coefficient recovery while allowing every unpaired marginal observation to contribute to coefficient estimation.
project_justification.fill: The population graph-completion theorem identifies the full coefficient equivalence class by edge residual diagonality plus coordinatewise positive-definite completion. The completion lemma proves \(\chi_G(q)>0\) exactly for completable data and \(|\chi_G(q)-\chi_G(q')|\le m\|q-q'\|_{\max}\) by translating feasible completions with \(E_G\). The graph covariance theorem uses simultaneous Gaussian operator-norm regions over all observed edges and marginals, a combined residual/completion feasibility score, and the existing path-product argument to prove inversion coverage, exclusion of graph-incompatible orders, a \(2L_B\bar r_n\) Hausdorff bound, exact graph-essential ancestry, and consistency. A one-edge specialization yields the generic two-view singleton corollary.

body.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the model anchor: its fully paired workflow uses cross-view disturbance diversity to identify shared causal structure, whereas the present claims concern only the narrower component-aligned Gaussian subclass and arbitrary graphs of paired covariance sources. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM and Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM motivate recursive residualization but do not establish removed-set path independence or partial-view positive-definite completion. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal and GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain use ICA structure or heterogeneity rather than selected paired covariance blocks. GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the classical chordal completion substrate; the signed arbitrary-graph completion value, its zero-fill Lipschitz proof, and its integration with LiMVAM residuals are derived here. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses recursive Schur updates and a score gap for one point-identified SEM, while GaoTaiAragam2022GaussianDAG studies point-identifying Gaussian-DAG estimation rather than set-valued graph compatibility. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian singular-value concentration and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies a general inversion comparison; neither gives the graph LiMVAM completion score or the explicit coefficient and path-product moduli. MohanPearl2021MissingData studies recoverability under missingness mechanisms, whereas the present sourcewise-iid common-population design assumes away selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN motivates a future MEG and fMRI diagnostic application but does not validate component alignment or the graph sampling assumptions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: All identification and inference results remain confined to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. Arbitrary-graph inference requires positive-definite covariance for every edge source and every marginal source, plus a fixed graph feasibility margin that explicitly rules out incompatible orders lying on the boundary \(\min_j\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})=0\). Exact ancestry additionally requires a fixed path-product margin. The sourcewise-iid samples must share one target population, although they need not be mutually independent. Generic pair identification is relative to a fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and supplies no uniform distance from its exceptional algebraic set. The \(2^p\)-state recursion counts exact-real arithmetic; duplicate-free numerical tuple enumeration beyond order enumeration is not claimed.
body.honest_scope: The arbitrary-view-graph completion theorem, signed completion margin, graph covariance-region inversion, generic calibration elbow, fixed-order recovery, removed-set recursion, and essential-poset conclusions apply only to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass with positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. They do not transfer to unrestricted LiMVAMs or establish the assumptions used by Heurtebise et al. Finite-sample coverage assumes sourcewise-iid edge and marginal samples from one target law, edge-joint and all-marginal positive definiteness, and no selection or transport. Hausdorff and exact-poset recovery are off the stated completion/residual and support boundaries. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain prospective diagnostic applications rather than empirical validation.
